newsitem.title: HAITI: Former Haitian president Aristide a proud father.
newsitem.headline: Former Haitian president Aristide a proud father.

text.p: Jean-Bertrand Aristide, the former priest who was Haiti's first freely elected president, became a father of a different sort on Friday night with the birth of his first child, a baby girl.

Mildred Trouillot Aristide, 34, the former president's wife of 10 months, gave birth to baby Christine at Canape-Vert Hospital in Port-au-Prince about 10 p.m. EST (1500 GMT), hospital officials said on Saturday.
Aristide, 43, emerged from the delivery room and announced the birth. The event brought high government officials and a party atmosphere to the hospital.
The hospital said mother and baby were in good condition after the birth, carried out via Caesarian section.
Haitian government officials, including President Rene Preval and Foreign Affairs Minister Fritz Longchamp, came to the hospital to congratulate the happy parents, who were married on Jan. 21.
A force of about 20,000 U.S.-led international troops occupied Haiti in September 1994, paving the way for Aristide's return to power after three years in exile following a bloody military coup.

Aristide, limited by the nation's constitution to serving one consecutive term, left the presidency in February 1996 with the inauguration of Preval, his successor. He was widely expected to seek Haiti's presidency again in 2000.
